title: Dummett’s principle and linearly ordered future cones

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic, Winter 2019/20 (notes dated January 2, 2020)
based_on.pages: §1.8, printed p.25, Example22; §2, printed p.27, Theorem11

summary: Characterize Dummett’s principle by comparable futures, place it above weak excluded middle, and derive its equivalent implication–disjunction schema.
abstract: Two possible futures may verify different statements without either future extending the other. Dummett’s principle asserts the disjunction of the two implications that compare those statements. We show that the principle holds for every valuation exactly when any two futures of the same world are comparable. It implies weak excluded middle, but a diamond separates the two principles and a chain still refutes full excluded middle. A second formulation lets an implication into a disjunction choose an implication to one side. We derive both formulations from one another in the original intuitionistic calculus, keeping every original assumption throughout.
